symbols.name: C
symbols.def: The number of mutually isolated sampled clusters.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The fixed number of units in every cluster.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: The fixed number of exact-count policies.

symbols.name: \mathcal A
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A=\mathcal K\), so one exact-count policy is selected.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: A schedule containing one binary potential outcome for every unit and every within-cluster assignment.

symbols.name: Y_j(z)
symbols.def: The outcome of unit \(j\) under within-cluster assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: An otherwise unrestricted law of the binary cluster schedule \(Y\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_K)\) is chosen before sampling and may lie on the boundary of \(\Delta_K\).

symbols.name: L_c
symbols.def: The first-stage label of cluster \(c\), generated according to exactly one of the regimes \(\mathsf B(p)\) and \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\).

symbols.name: Z_c
symbols.def: The realized within-cluster assignment of cluster \(c\), generated conditionally on \(L_c\) by the active randomization regime.

symbols.name: O_c^{\mathrm{hit}}
symbols.def: The record retaining \((L_c,Z_c)\), retaining the observed outcome vector when \(Z_c\in\bigcup_{k\in\mathcal K}\mathcal S_k\), and replacing it by \(\star\) otherwise.

symbols.name: \mathcal L
symbols.def: A bounded loss \(\mathcal L(U,a)\) depending on the schedule law only through \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_K)\).

symbols.name: \widehat U^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,k}
symbols.def: \(\widehat U^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,k}=\bigl(\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}\bigr)^{-1}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}W_c(Z_c)\), with fallback \(1/2\) when the denominator is zero.

symbols.name: \mathsf B(p)
symbols.def: Independently draw \(L_c\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(p)\), then conditionally assign the coordinates of \(Z_c\) independently as \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_{L_c})\).

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: \(\alpha_k=\lim_{C\to\infty}C_{C,k}/C\), whenever the displayed limit is invoked.

symbols.name: \mathsf{CR}(\alpha)
symbols.def: Draw \(L=(L_1,\ldots,L_C)\) uniformly over label vectors with exactly \(C_{C,k}\) copies of label \(k\), then conditionally draw \(Z_c\) uniformly on \(\mathcal S_{L_c}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak D_C
symbols.def: All measurable randomized rules mapping the indicated experiment to one action in \(\mathcal A\).

symbols.name: P_0
symbols.def: A schedule law whose assignment-specific outcome-vector marginals have positive average variance on each active target slice.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: \(h=(h_k)_{k\in A}\) is a target contrast displacement.

symbols.name: P_{0,z}
symbols.def: The \(P_0\)-marginal law of the observed outcome vector under assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: P_{t,h,z}
symbols.def: For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), \(k\in A\), it satisfies \(dP_{t,h,z}/dP_{0,z}(y)=\exp\{t h_k(W(y)-\mu_z)/\tau_k^2-\Lambda_{z,k}(t h_k/\tau_k^2)\}\); nontarget marginals equal \(P_{0,z}\).

symbols.name: \underline\tau
symbols.def: A fixed lower bound for active calibrated slice standard deviations.

symbols.name: v_A
symbols.def: \(v_A=(v_k)_{k\in A}\), with \(v_k=\tau_k^2(P_0)\) in the exact-hit application.

symbols.name: r_A
symbols.def: \(r_A=(r_k)_{k\in A}\); inactive coordinates are not arguments of the face game.

symbols.name: G_A(v_A,r_A)
symbols.def: \(G_A(v_A,r_A)=\inf_\delta\sup_{h\in H_A}\mathbb E_h[\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_{\delta(X)}]\), where independently \(X_k=h_k+\sqrt{v_k/r_k}Z_k\) and \(Z_k\sim N(0,1)\); it is \(+\infty\) if any active \(r_k=0\).

symbols.name: s_{A,\max}
symbols.type: largest active hit mass of one nominal label

symbols.name: t
symbols.type: first nominal-label share for two policies

symbols.name: \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}
symbols.def: The empirical second moment of all \(K\) calibrated influence coordinates, using estimated hit rates under \(\mathsf B(p)\) and the fixed shares \(C_{C,k}/C\) under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), with the prespecified bounded fallback on undefined cells.

symbols.name: \mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)
symbols.type: simultaneous confidence set for policy rank
symbols.def: Invert all studentized pairwise intervals from the calibrated estimates and \(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\); return \(\{1,\ldots,K\}\) if a required target assignment cell is empty.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: The requested deterministic gap between the Gaussian upper and lower certificates.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: A fixed radius for bounded subsets of the active tangent space.

symbols.name: \delta_{\varepsilon,A}
symbols.def: A measurable posterior-mean selector from an \(\varepsilon\)-least-favourable finite prior on a translation-normalized contrast grid, with a certified truncation tail bound.

symbols.name: L_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)
symbols.def: The finite-prior Bayes value minus certified quadrature and truncation errors.

symbols.name: U_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)
symbols.def: The global simple-regret upper bound for \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\), including certified grid, quadrature, and Gaussian-tail errors.

symbols.name: \mathfrak C_K
symbols.def: Combine facewise truncation certificates with adaptive refinement across changing active faces and covariance limits, then apply coordinatewise branch-and-bound over \(B\Delta_K\) and \(\Delta_A\).

symbols.name: R_{B,p}
symbols.space: \(\text{Markov kernels from schedules to observed records}\)
symbols.def: The known kernel that draws \(L\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(p)\), draws the coordinates of \(Z\) independently as \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_L)\), and returns \(O=(L,Z,Y(Z))\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{hit}}(p)
symbols.def: The image of \((Q^B_{P,p})^{\otimes C}\) under coordinatewise reduction \(O_c\mapsto O_c^{\mathrm{hit}}\).

symbols.name: R^{CR}_{C_C}
symbols.space: \(\text{Markov kernels from schedule arrays to observed arrays}\)
symbols.def: The known kernel that draws a label vector uniformly with counts \(C_C=(C_{C,k})_k\), conditionally draws \(Z_c\) uniformly on \(\mathcal S_{L_c}\), and returns \((O_c)_{c=1}^C\).

symbols.name: Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}
symbols.def: \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}=P^{\otimes C}R^{CR}_{C_C}\); conditionally on the randomized fixed-count label vector, it is the product of its stratum-specific observed laws.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha)=Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}\), indexed by the fixed count vector \(C_C=(C_{C,k})_{k\in\mathcal K}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{hit}}(\alpha)
symbols.def: The image of \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}\) that retains each realized exact-count assignment and outcome vector while deleting the randomized label vector.

symbols.name: \bar P_{t,h}
symbols.def: \(\bar P_{t,h}=\bigotimes_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}P_{t,h,z}\); at \(t=0\), \(\bar P_0\) and \(P_0\) induce the same observed law under either regime.

symbols.name: \widehat\Sigma_{C,A}
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}=(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)})_{AA}\) whenever the full estimator is defined, or the same empirical score construction restricted directly to active coordinates.

assumptions.condition: \(Y_c(z)\) is invariant to assignments outside cluster \(c\).
\((L_1,\ldots,L_C)\) is uniform over label vectors satisfying \(\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k\}=C_{C,k}\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K\).

standard.name: First-stage complete randomization with fixed label counts
Stable positive treatment fractions in complete randomization
Uniform nondegeneracy of limiting contrast variances
Stable positive treatment fractions for all reported strata
Uniform nondegeneracy of all reported contrast variances

definitions.name: mutually exclusive assignment regimes
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf B(p)\) draws iid categorical labels and conditionally independent unit assignments, whereas \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\) draws one fixed-count label vector and conditionally uniform exact-slice assignments; every result invokes exactly one regime.

definitions.name: schedule-to-observation laws
definitions.construction: In regime \(\mathsf B(p)\), \(Q^B_{P,p}=P R_{B,p}\) and the sample law is \((Q^B_{P,p})^{\otimes C}\). In regime \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}=P^{\otimes C}R^{CR}_{C_C}\), equivalently the conditional product of stratum-specific observed laws given the randomized fixed-count label vector.

definitions.name: full and reduced regime experiments
definitions.construction: \((\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{full}}(p),\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{hit}}(p))\) are \((Q^B_{P,p})^{\otimes C}\) and its target-hit image; \((\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha),\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{hit}}(\alpha))\) are \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}\) and its label-deleted image.

definitions.name: assignment-calibrated exact-hit estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widetilde U_C=(\widetilde U_{C,k})_{k\in\mathcal K}\), where \(\widetilde U_{C,k}=M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\overline W_z\); \(\widetilde U_{C,A}\) is its active-face restriction, with the prespecified empty-cell values inherited from \(\overline W_z\).

definitions.name: raw cross-label pooled-hit estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat U^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,k}\) is the ratio of the sum of observed cluster welfares on \(\mathcal S_k\) to the number of hits on \(\mathcal S_k\), with fallback \(1/2\) on a zero denominator.

definitions.name: published nominal-label estimator and efficient nominal subexperiment
definitions.construction: Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is the Horvitz--Thompson estimator \(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}=(Cp_k)^{-1}\sum_c\mathbf 1\{L_c=k\}[\gamma_k(Z_c)/\beta_k(Z_c)]W_c(Z_c)\). The best regular nominal-label procedure calibrates assignment cells using only \(\{L_c=k,Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}\) and has canonical gradient \(\phi_k^{nom}\).

definitions.name: explicit target tangent and least-favourable submodel
definitions.construction: Set \(\bar P_0=\bigotimes_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}P_{0,z}\), keep nontarget marginals fixed, use \(dP_{t,h,z}/dP_{0,z}(y)=\exp\{t h_k(W(y)-\mu_z)/\tau_k^2-\Lambda_{z,k}(t h_k/\tau_k^2)\}\) for \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), \(k\in A\), define \(\bar P_{t,h}=\bigotimes_zP_{t,h,z}\), and set \(\bar P_{C,h}=\bar P_{C^{-1/2},h}\).

definitions.name: face-projected Gaussian simple-regret game
definitions.construction: \(G_A(v_A,r_A)=\inf_\delta\sup_{h\in H_A}\mathbb E_h[\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_{\delta(X)}]\) for independent \(X_k\sim N(h_k,v_k/r_k)\), defined only for positive active \(v_A,r_A\) and extended by \(+\infty\) if an active \(r_k=0\).

definitions.name: tie-aware rank target and calibrated confidence set
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Rank}_k(U)=\{1+\sum_{j\neq k}\mathbf 1\{U_j>U_k\},\ldots,K-\sum_{j\neq k}\mathbf 1\{U_j<U_k\}\}\), and \(\mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)\) is the max-\(t\) inversion with the full-rank empty-cell fallback.

definitions.name: attained fixed-face Gaussian certificate
definitions.construction: On a translation-normalized contrast box, solve the finite zero-sum game between a rational contrast grid and randomized actions; extend its least-favourable-prior selector to \(H_A\), and bound omitted contrasts, Gaussian quadrature, and grid interpolation explicitly to compute \(L_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)\) and \(U_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)\).

definitions.name: uniform covariance-boundary handle
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_K\): couple the fixed-face certificates across changing active faces and covariance limits, then refine branch-and-bound cells over \(B\Delta_K\) and \(\Delta_A\).

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), for every \(k,\ell\in\mathcal K\) and \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), \(\Pr(L_c=\ell,Z_c=z)=p_\ell B_{k\ell}/M_k\), \(\Pr(Z_c=z)=q_k/M_k\), and \(\Pr(L_c=\ell\mid Z_c=z)=p_\ell B_{k\ell}/q_k\). Hence \(Z_c\mid\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}\) is uniform on \(\mathcal S_k\), and the target-hit count vector is multinomial with probabilities \((q_1,\ldots,q_K,1-\sum_kq_k)\).
statements.justification: This factorization identifies the Bernoulli information carrier and the cross-label hit rate.
statements.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 Appendix B retains the nominally matching label rather than the pooled carrier with rate \(Bp\).
statements.consumer: The Bernoulli estimator, lower experiment, and nominal-label allocation all use this factorization.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(C\), \(p\), and bounded target-only loss \(\mathcal L\), regime \(\mathsf B(p)\) satisfies \[\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{full}}(p)))] = \inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{hit}}(p)))].\] The equality persists after deleting \(L_c\) conditional on every realized target assignment. It holds for rules observing the entire outcome vector because the reverse inequality fixes every nontarget assignment marginal at a known distribution and replaces the unidentified schedule coupling by the product of its assignment-specific marginals.
statements.justification: This all-rule equality isolates exactly which Bernoulli observations can carry worst-case information about the target.
statements.gap: No named comparator proves a finite-sample all-measurable-rule deletion equivalence over unrestricted assignment-specific schedule marginals.
statements.consumer: It licenses the full-experiment local minimax lower bound without a spillover response model.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(C\), fixed label-count vector, and bounded target-only loss \(\mathcal L\), regime \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\) satisfies \[\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha)))] = \inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{hit}}(\alpha)))].\] Here the reduced experiment deletes the randomized label vector after the realized exact-count assignments are recorded.
statements.justification: The exact-count benchmark must be stated as its own randomization experiment.
statements.gap: Two-stage design papers retain strategy labels, while the exact count itself identifies the target slice in this menu.
statements.consumer: This gives the clean exact-count experiment used as the mechanism benchmark.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), \(\phi_k^B\in L^2_0(Q^B_{P_0,p})\) is the canonical gradient of \(U_k\), with variance \(\tau_k^2/q_k\) and zero covariance across distinct slices. The full calibrated vector satisfies \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_B^{(K)}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_B^{(K)}.\] Its active restriction has covariance \(\Sigma_{B,A}=(\Sigma_B^{(K)})_{AA}\).
statements.justification: This derives the full-vector calibrated score and primitive Bernoulli CLT that underlie the headline mechanism comparison.
statements.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is a nominal-label Horvitz--Thompson construction rather than the pooled assignment-calibrated canonical gradient.
statements.consumer: Every realized exact hit can contribute to full-menu welfare estimation and active-face policy selection.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\) with \(\alpha_k>0\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), the full calibrated vector satisfies \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}.\] Conditionally on the fixed-count label vector, its triangular-array influence coordinates are \(\phi_{c,k}^{CR}\).
statements.justification: This supplies the full-menu exact-count benchmark only when every reported policy receives a positive limiting share.
statements.gap: Existing two-stage variance formulas target direct and spillover contrasts rather than the full calibrated exact-slice welfare vector.
statements.consumer: It supports full-menu covariance estimation and rank inference under the benchmark mechanism.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), if \(\alpha_k>0\) only for every \(k\in A\), then \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_{CR,A}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\to_P\Sigma_{CR,A}.\] No estimator or covariance limit is asserted for an unallocated inactive policy.
statements.justification: The mechanism game needs only the positively allocated active tie face.
statements.gap: The full-menu CR limit is undefined at inactive zero-share coordinates; this proposition isolates the valid face experiment.
statements.consumer: It supplies the active covariance used by LAN, mechanism comparison, and oracle transfer.

statements.statement: Fix \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), and write \(\eta_k=p_kB_{kk}\). Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is exactly \[\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}=\frac{1}{Cp_k}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k\}\frac{\gamma_k(Z_c)}{\beta_k(Z_c)}W_c(Z_c)=\frac{1}{C\eta_k}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k,Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}W_c(Z_c).\] It has influence function \(\phi_k^{HOS}=\eta_k^{-1}\mathbf 1\{L=k,Z\in\mathcal S_k\}W(Z)-U_k\) and \[\operatorname{AVAR}(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k})=\frac{\tau_k^2+b_k^2}{\eta_k}+U_k^2\left(\frac1{\eta_k}-1\right).\] The best regular estimator in the nominal-label-\(k\) subexperiment has canonical gradient \(\phi_k^{nom}\) and efficiency bound \(\tau_k^2/\eta_k\). Therefore, whenever \(q_k>\eta_k\) and \(\tau_k^2>0\), \[\frac{\tau_k^2}{q_k}<\frac{\tau_k^2}{p_kB_{kk}}\leq\operatorname{AVAR}(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}).\] If \(b_k^2>0\), assignment-cell calibration within the nominal subexperiment is itself strictly more efficient than Eq. (S1), apart from the additional Horvitz--Thompson participation term displayed above.
statements.justification: This makes the closest same-target comparison exact at the estimator, influence-function, and variance levels.
statements.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 Appendix B proves unbiasedness of Eq. (S1) but does not derive the pooled efficient bound or separate its cell-heterogeneity and Horvitz--Thompson participation losses.
statements.consumer: Analysts can quantify both the cross-label gain and the additional gain from assignment-cell calibration over the published estimator.

statements.statement: In regime \(\mathsf B(p)\), the raw pooled estimator has influence function \(\psi_k\) and asymptotic variance \(\rho_k^2/q_k=(\tau_k^2+b_k^2)/q_k\). It is efficient if and only if \(b_k^2=0\). At \(n=4\), count-one assignment means \((4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5)\) give \(U_1=1/2\), \(\tau_1^2=4/25\), \(\rho_1^2=1/4\), and excess \(9/100\) before division by \(q_1\).
statements.justification: The variance decomposition identifies the exact calibration correction.
statements.gap: The supporting decomposition distinguishes within-slice assignment heterogeneity from the separate Horvitz--Thompson participation loss in HanOwusuShin2026 Eq. (S1).
statements.consumer: It tells analysts when raw pooling is safe and when cell calibration is necessary.

statements.statement: Let \(A=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_kU_k(P_0)\), with \(|A|\geq2\), and let every policy in \(A^c\) be separated from the tied active welfare. Set \(\bar P_0=\bigotimes_zP_{0,z}\) and use \(\bar P_{C,h}=\bar P_{C^{-1/2},h}\), \(h\in H_A\). Then \(Q^B_{\bar P_0,p}=Q^B_{P_0,p}\), \(dU_k(\bar P_{t,h})/dt|_{t=0}=h_k\), \(\dot\ell_k^B\in L^2_0(Q^B_{P_0,p})\), and \[\log\frac{d(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}{d(Q^B_{P_0,p})^{\otimes C}}=h^{\prime}\Delta_C^B-\tfrac12h^{\prime}I_Bh+o_{(Q^B_{P_0,p})^{\otimes C}}(1),\qquad \Delta_C^B\Rightarrow N(0,I_B).\] The active estimator limit is \(X_k=h_k+\sqrt{\tau_k^2/q_k}Z_k\), with covariance \(\Sigma_{B,A}\). For every measurable randomized rule sequence \(\delta_C\), \[\lim_{M\to\infty}\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{h\in H_A:\lVert h\rVert\leq M}\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})]\geq G_A(\tau_A^2,q_A).\] The same bound holds for rules observing the full Bernoulli experiment by nuisance deletion.
statements.justification: The explicit score turns the hit map into an all-rule lower experiment without a DQM placeholder.
statements.gap: HiranoPorter2009 gives the general limit-experiment architecture but not this nuisance-deleted exact-hit score or face experiment.
statements.consumer: It proves that nontarget observations cannot erase Bernoulli mechanism loss under unrestricted schedules.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), the product-coupled exponential tilt satisfies \(Q^{CR}_{\bar P_0,C_C}=Q^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}\). Conditionally on the fixed-count label vector, \(\dot\ell_{c,k}^{CR}\) lies in the corresponding stratum observed \(L^2_0\) space and \[\log\frac{dQ^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}{dQ^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}}=h^{\prime}\Delta_C^{CR}-\tfrac12h^{\prime}I_{CR}h+o_{Q^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}}(1),\qquad \Delta_C^{CR}\Rightarrow N(0,I_{CR}).\] The active limit is \(X_k=h_k+\sqrt{\tau_k^2/\alpha_k}Z_k\), with covariance \(\Sigma_{CR,A}\), and every measurable randomized rule sequence satisfies \[\lim_{M\to\infty}\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{h\in H_A:\lVert h\rVert\leq M}\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{Q^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})]\geq G_A(\tau_A^2,\alpha_A).\] The independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) target-bit witness is a separate submodel with \(\tau_k^2=1/4\) and information \(4\alpha_k\).
statements.justification: The exact-count regime requires its own triangular-array LAN statement and information matrix.
statements.gap: Generic treatment-rule LAN theory does not derive this fixed-stratum exact-slice experiment.
statements.consumer: It supplies the all-rule exact-count benchmark used in optimized mechanism comparison.

statements.statement: When \(K=2\) and \(A=\mathcal K\), choosing the larger calibrated estimate attains \(\kappa\sqrt{\tau_1^2/q_1+\tau_2^2/q_2}\) under \(\mathsf B(p)\) and \(\kappa\sqrt{\tau_1^2/\alpha_1+\tau_2^2/\alpha_2}\) under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\). The optimized exact-count share is \(\alpha_1^\star=\sqrt{v_1}/(\sqrt{v_1}+\sqrt{v_2})\). If \(B_{11}>B_{12}\) and \(B_{22}>B_{21}\), then \(t^\star=0\) exactly when \(v_1/v_2\leq(B_{22}-B_{21})B_{12}^2/[(B_{11}-B_{12})B_{22}^2]\), \(t^\star=1\) exactly when \(v_1/v_2\geq(B_{22}-B_{21})B_{11}^2/[(B_{11}-B_{12})B_{21}^2]\), and otherwise equals \[\frac{B_{22}\sqrt{v_1(B_{11}-B_{12})/[v_2(B_{22}-B_{21})]}-B_{12}}{(B_{11}-B_{12})+(B_{22}-B_{21})\sqrt{v_1(B_{11}-B_{12})/[v_2(B_{22}-B_{21})]}}.\] For \(n=4\), \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(1/4,1/2)\), and equal variances, \(B=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}27/64&1/4\\27/128&3/8\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\), \(t^\star=0.39383577843\ldots\), the regret ratio is \(1.26189430297\ldots\), and the cluster-count ratio is \(1.59237723186\ldots\).
statements.justification: This gives the exact constant, full allocation map, and reproducible four-node kill test.
statements.gap: Stoye2009 and Joo2025 do not map a common exact-slice target through the binomial hit matrix.
statements.consumer: A two-saturation pilot can compute its optimal nominal share and excess cluster requirement.

statements.statement: For every tie face \(A\) with \(|A|\geq2\) and positive \(v_A\), define \(s_A(p)=\sum_{k\in A}(Bp)_k\), \(a_A(p)=(Bp)_A/s_A(p)\), and \(s_{A,\max}=\max_\ell\sum_{k\in A}B_{k\ell}\). Then \(G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A)=s_A(p)^{-1/2}G_A(v_A,a_A(p))\) and \[\frac{R_{B,A}^\star(v_A)}{R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)}\geq s_{A,\max}^{-1/2}>1.\] Equality in this lower ratio holds exactly when there exists a Bernoulli optimizer \(p\) supported on columns attaining \(s_{A,\max}\) whose normalized active vector \(a_A(p)\) is exact-count optimal. Inactive coordinates may be zero and are never passed to \(G_A\).
statements.justification: This sole headline theorem gives the corrected face-specific optimized mechanism-deficiency and exact equality frontier.
statements.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 and power-optimal saturation-design papers do not give an all-rule facewise information-loss frontier for the same exact-count deployment target.
statements.consumer: It gives a prospective lower bound on the clusters needed by a Bernoulli implementation at any partial tie.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), \(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_B^{(K)}\), and \[\liminf_{C\to\infty}\inf_{P:\min_k\tau_k^2(P)\geq\underline\tau^2}\Pr_P\{\operatorname{Rank}_k(U)\subseteq\mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)\text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K\}\geq1-\gamma.\] The assertion is uniform over partial ties. The full-rank empty-cell fallback is always defined, and its activation probability is at most \(\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}M_k\exp(-Cq_k/M_k)\).
statements.justification: This states the correct set-valued rank target at ties.
statements.gap: MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024 begins from a joint approximation and does not derive calibrated random-hit scores.
statements.consumer: Bernoulli saturation studies obtain simultaneous winner and rank uncertainty.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), with \(\alpha_k>0\) and nondegenerate slice variance for every reported \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}\), and \[\liminf_{C\to\infty}\inf_{P:\min_{k\in\mathcal K}\tau_k^2(P)\geq\underline\tau^2}\Pr_P\{\operatorname{Rank}_k(U)\subseteq\mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)\text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K\}\geq1-\gamma,\] uniformly over partial ties.
statements.justification: The complete-randomization rank theorem is separate from the Bernoulli hit-count theorem.
statements.gap: Generic two-stage Wald theory does not state set-valued exact-slice rank coverage at partial ties.
statements.consumer: Exact-count studies can report rank ranges under their actual fixed allocation.

statements.statement: For every fixed face \(A\), positive \(v_A,r_A\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), the finite-grid least-favourable-prior construction returns a measurable selector \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\) and computable outward-rounded certificates satisfying \[L_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)\leq G_A(v_A,r_A)\leq U_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A),\qquad U_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)-L_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)\leq\varepsilon.\] Coordinatewise branch-and-bound with this static Gaussian oracle certifies the outer problems over \(B\Delta_K\) and \(\Delta_A\). For \(n=6\), \(A=\mathcal K\), \((m_1,m_2,m_3)=(1,2,4)\), and \(v_A=(1/4,1/5,1/8)\), \[B=\begin{pmatrix}3125/7776&64/243&4/243\\3125/15552&80/243&20/243\\125/15552&20/243&80/243\end{pmatrix}.\] Outward-rounded interval arithmetic certifies a Bernoulli optimizer in \(p_1^\star\in[0,1/50]\), \(p_2^\star\in[39/50,41/50]\), \(p_3^\star\in[4/25,11/50]\), and a CR optimizer in \(\alpha_1^\star\in[9/25,2/5]\), \(\alpha_2^\star\in[33/100,19/50]\), \(\alpha_3^\star\in[1/4,29/100]\). The rational allocations \(p=(0,4/5,1/5)\) and \(\alpha=(19/50,7/20,27/100)\) are certified \(1/200\)-optimal. The optimized risks obey \(R_{B,A}^\star\in[67/200,73/200]\), \(R_{CR,A}^\star\in[53/200,57/200]\), and \[R_{B,A}^\star/R_{CR,A}^\star\in[1217/1000,73/53].\] The unique maximum-mass column is column two, with \(s_{A,\max}=164/243\) and normalized active vector \((16/41,20/41,5/41)\), which lies outside the certified CR optimizer box; the equality condition in the headline theorem therefore fails. The boundary Bernoulli optimizer and unequal CR shares are not symmetry-forced and display substantive coupling through \(B\Delta_K\).
statements.justification: This supplies a non-symmetric, attained, and reproducible general-menu design certificate tied to the calibrated cluster experiment.
statements.gap: Joo2025 informs the static Gaussian selector, but does not couple it to the exact-hit polytope, certify the outer saturation design, or transfer it to calibrated cluster data.
statements.consumer: A designer with three asymmetric candidate saturations receives certified optimizer boxes, implementable rational allocations, and a mechanism-risk ratio.

statements.statement: Fix \(A\), positive \(v_A\), and \(M<\infty\). Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), estimate \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\) on an independent sample split, compute \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\), and apply it to the remaining \(\widetilde U_{C,A}\). Uniformly over \(h\in H_A\) with \(\lVert h\rVert\leq M\), its scaled simple regret has limit superior at most \(U_\varepsilon(v_A,(Bp)_A)\); with a vanishing split fraction and \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), it attains the certified Gaussian value.
statements.justification: This is the required oracle-to-data attainment result for the Bernoulli mechanism.
statements.gap: Gaussian decision certificates are not useful for this experiment without a uniform calibrated-score transfer.
statements.consumer: It turns the computed selector into an implementable Bernoulli saturation-design rule.

statements.statement: Fix \(A\), positive \(v_A\), and \(M<\infty\). Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), estimate \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\) on a prespecified within-stratum split, compute \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\), and apply it to the remaining \(\widetilde U_{C,A}\). Uniformly over \(h\in H_A\) with \(\lVert h\rVert\leq M\), its scaled simple regret has limit superior at most \(U_\varepsilon(v_A,\alpha_A)\); with a vanishing split fraction and \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), it attains the certified Gaussian value.
statements.justification: This is the separate oracle-to-data attainment result for exact-count complete randomization.
statements.gap: The fixed-stratum primitive experiment needs its own transfer rather than borrowing an iid Bernoulli argument.
statements.consumer: It implements the certified selector under the benchmark mechanism.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak C_K\), construct one adaptive certificate whose error bound is uniform when the active face changes, active variances approach admissible nondegenerate limits, or inactive design coordinates vanish, while never evaluating \(G_A\) at a zero active rate. Determine whether a single branch-and-bound schedule can certify all partial-tie faces and covariance perturbations simultaneously over a compact primitive class.
statements.justification: The fixed positive-face computation is attained; uniform coordination across changing faces remains the genuinely open theorem.
statements.gap: Neither Joo2025 nor Kato2026 treats this static exact-hit polytope with vanishing inactive coordinates and data-dependent face changes.
statements.consumer: A universal implementation could certify one design before the analyst knows which welfare ties are locally relevant.

sampling_model.design: Exactly one regime is active. In \(\mathsf B(p)\), labels are iid categorical and units are conditionally independent Bernoulli. In \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), the label vector has fixed counts \(C_{C,k}\) and each cluster is conditionally uniform on its exact-count slice.
sampling_model.units: Observe \(C\) independent equal-size cluster schedules from an unrestricted binary potential-outcome law, with no interference across clusters and arbitrary interference within a cluster.
sampling_model.treatment: The schedule law \(P\) is mapped to observed data by the known kernel \(R_{B,p}\) or the joint fixed-count kernel \(R^{CR}_{C_C}\); scores and influence functions live in the induced observed-law spaces.
sampling_model.overlap: Interior rational saturations make every Bernoulli hit rate positive. Active-face CR results require positive shares only on \(A\); the full-vector CR CLT and all-policy rank theorem require \(\alpha_k>0\) for every reported policy.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate assignment-specific means and variances within realized target cells, average cells uniformly within each exact-count slice, and use a prespecified bounded fallback for empty cells. Covariance-driven selection may use sample splitting.

estimand_functional: \(\widetilde U_C=(M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\overline W_z)_{k\in\mathcal K}\), with full covariance \(\Sigma_B^{(K)}\) under \(\mathsf B(p)\) and \(\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}\) under all-positive-share \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Appendix-B Eq. (S1), transcribed in the present notation, is the Horvitz--Thompson estimator \(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}=(Cp_k)^{-1}\sum_c\mathbf 1\{L_c=k\}[\gamma_k(Z_c)/\beta_k(Z_c)]W_c(Z_c)\).
A one-shot Gaussian best-arm selector is characterized using least-favourable-prior methods.
Minimum-\(L^2\) off-policy transport weights are obtained by Fourier projection under structured interference.
An adaptive sequential fixed-budget best-arm strategy is asymptotically minimax and Bayes optimal for simple regret.
Randomized saturation shares are optimized for power to estimate direct and spillover effects.
Simultaneous rank confidence sets are constructed by inverting joint pairwise comparisons.
Joint covariance estimators and Wald procedures are derived for vectors of two-stage causal effects.
Finite-sample two-treatment minimax-regret rules are certified through a statistical game and least-favourable priors.

tldr: The headline result prices the loss from implementing exact-count policy ranking through Bernoulli labels: after projecting to any tied-best face, the optimized regret ratio is bounded by the active exact-hit mass and has an exact equality frontier. Separate observed-law theorems establish finite-sample nuisance deletion, full-menu calibrated CLTs, active-face LAN lower experiments, and tie-valid rank inference. The closest same-target estimator is transcribed exactly from Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1); its derived influence variance reveals cross-label, assignment-cell, and Horvitz--Thompson participation losses. A non-symmetric three-policy menu with unequal variances supplies certified optimizer boxes, attained Gaussian risks, and calibrated oracle-to-data transfer. Uniform certification across changing faces and covariance boundaries remains open.

project_justification.gap: Same-target saturation-ranking work uses the nominal-label Horvitz--Thompson estimator in Appendix-B Eq. (S1) and a rule-specific regret envelope; it does not give all-rule nuisance deletion, observed-law target tangents, or a face-specific optimized mechanism-deficiency frontier.
project_justification.niche: Exact-count deployment exposes a known hit polytope \(B\Delta_K\) inside an unrestricted interference model, allowing the assignment mechanism itself to be priced for the same causal target while keeping schedule and observed-data laws distinct.
project_justification.fill: The project makes mechanism loss the sole headline, derives its observed-score and efficiency foundations, proves the exact Han variance comparison, and couples a Joo-informed static Gaussian selector to calibrated cluster data and a certified asymmetric outer design.

related_work: HanOwusuShin2026 is the closest same-target paper. Its Appendix-B Eq. (S1), pp. 40--44, uses the Horvitz--Thompson normalization \(1/(Cp_k)\) and a within-label likelihood ratio; the exact comparison theorem derives its influence variance and strictly refines it through cross-label assignment calibration. HiranoPorter2009 supplies the limit-experiment architecture, but the all-rule nuisance-deletion theorem and legal observed-law exact-hit tangent are specific to this model. BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 makes saturation shares a design object under a power criterion rather than optimized facewise simple regret. Joo2025 informs the static Gaussian selector; the contribution here is its coupling to the exact-hit polytope, certified asymmetric outer design, and calibrated cluster-data transfer, not a new generic Gaussian minimax construction. Kato2026, arXiv:2506.24007v6 dated 25 July 2026, is Masahiro Kato's adaptive sequential best-arm comparator and only informs the certification architecture. LoombaEckles2026 informs score projection under structured interference. JiangImaiMalani2023 and MogstadRomanoShaikhWilhelm2024 inform the supporting covariance and rank-inversion results. ChanNakamuraSakaiForastiere2023 is nonarchival prior use of cross-label information for a different hypothetical-allocation target. EggerHaushoferMiguelNiehausWalker2022 supplies the prospective Kenya saturation-design consumer.
technical_internal_limitation: Raw hit pooling is not universally efficient when assignment-specific means vary inside an exact-count slice. The four count-one assignment means \((4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5)\) yield \(\rho_1^2=1/4\) and \(\tau_1^2=4/25\). Han--Owusu--Shin Eq. (S1) additionally pays the first-stage Horvitz--Thompson participation term \(U_k^2(1/\eta_k-1)\). The independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) target-bit witness instead has \(\tau_k^2=1/4\) and information \(4q_k\); it is a special lower-bound witness, not the general exponential-tilt score construction.
honest_scope: The results concern fixed \(n\), fixed \(K\), equal cluster sizes, distinct interior rational saturations, isolated iid cluster schedules, and exact-slice welfare. Bernoulli-label and exact-count complete randomization are mutually exclusive regimes, and all scores are defined under their induced observed laws. Active-face CR results allow zero inactive shares, but the full-menu CR CLT and rank theorem require every reported share to be positive. At a unique best policy first-order local regret is zero. When \(K=2\), the face game reduces to the classical sign rule and Neyman allocation; assignment-homogeneous slice means eliminate the calibration component but not necessarily the Horvitz--Thompson participation term in Eq. (S1). The finite positive-face Gaussian certificate and asymmetric three-policy design are theorem targets. A single certificate uniform across data-dependent face changes, covariance perturbations, and admissible boundary limits remains open. The Kenya design is a prospective design consumer rather than an authorized reanalysis.
